;Armed conflicts and attacks 
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[August 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***At least seven [[Afghan National Police|policemen]] are killed and 15 others injured after a [[car bomb]] explodes outside a police station in [[Ghazni]], [[Afghanistan]]. As yet nobody has claimed responsibility. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/7-police-killed-ghazni-car-bomb-security-source (TOLONews)]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***Afghanistan's [[Loya Jirga]] approves to release 400 "hard-core" [[Taliban]] prisoners after deliberation. Afghan President [[Ashraf Ghani]] says he will sign the order and that doing this, the Afghan government complies with the Taliban demand of freeing prisoners to start intra-Afghan peace talks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban/afghanistan-to-release-400-hard-core-taliban-to-start-peace-talks-idUSKCN25507I (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Maghreb insurgency]]
**[[Kouré shooting]]
***Six [[French people|French]] aid workers, their driver, and a local guide are shot dead by gunmen in an attack on a group of [[aid workers]] in [[Kouré, Niger|Kouré]], [[Tillabéri Region|Tillabéri]], [[Niger]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53716588 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
**State-run oil company [[Saudi Aramco]] reports that profits in the first half of 2020 plunged by 50% compared to the same period last year, with decreased demand in oil caused by COVID-19 cited as the main reason by CEO [[Amin H. Nasser]]. The company plans to uphold its promise of paying out [[United States dollar|US$]]75 billion in annual [[dividend]]s in spite of this. [https://apnews.com/42db464bb1af2f8f7a891baf18f3da26 (AP)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Sparta earthquake]]
**An earthquake with a magnitude of 5.1 hits near the small town of [[Sparta, North Carolina|Sparta]], [[North Carolina]]. Shaking was felt throughout the [[East Coast of the United States|U.S. East Coast]], though no damage and injuries are reported. The earthquake is the largest in the state since 1916. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/51-magnitude-earthquake-north-carolina-virginia-border/story?id=72266987 (ABC News)]
*[[2020 Vijayawada fire]]
**At least 11 people are dead and 22 others injured in a fire at a COVID-19 facility centre in India's [[Andhra Pradesh]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/deadly-fire-coronavirus-facility-south-india-200809064454139.html (Al Jazeera)]
*Eight people are dead after [[floods]] caused by [[thunderstorms]] and torrential rains affected [[Euboea|Evia]], [[Greece]]. Dozens of people have been evacuated from the area. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53714286 (BBC News)][https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6872880/death-toll-from-greek-storm-rises-to-eight/ (''Canberra Times'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports Australia's deadliest day since the pandemic began in the country, with 17 deaths reported aside from 394 new [[COVID-19]] cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/aug/09/victoria-records-17-coronavirus-deaths-on-australias-deadliest-day-of-pandemic-so-far (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] marks 100 days without community transmission of COVID-19. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12354489 (''The New Zealand Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[National Public Health Organization (Greece)|National Public Health Organization]] reports 203 new COVID-19 cases in Greece in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single day for the country since the pandemic began. [https://greece.greekreporter.com/2020/08/09/new-coronavirus-cases-jump-to-a-record-high-203-in-greece/ (Greek Reporter)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]] 
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 1,062 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. It is the first time that the country has recorded more than 1,000 new cases since late June. [https://www.itv.com/news/2020-08-09/coronavirus-uk-fatalities-increase-by-eight-bringing-total-death-toll-to-46574 (ITV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[India]] reports its highest single day record of 64,399 new cases in the last 24 hours. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/record-64399-new-covid-19-cases-861-deaths-in-india/articleshow/77442348.cms (''Times of India'')]

;Law and crime
**A teenager is killed and 20 others are shot, including an off-duty police officer, in a [[mass shooting]] at a large gathering in [[Southeast (Washington, D.C.)|Southeast Washington, D.C.]] Police are searching for at least three shooters. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/09/us/washington-dc-shooting/index.html (CNN)]
*A 17-year-old [[Chili's]] hostess is hospitalized after being attacked at a Chili's restaurant in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]], after telling a large group of women that they may not share a table due to safety regulations regarding the coronavirus. The hostess has no plans to return to the Chili's restaurant where she was attacked. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/chili-s-teen-hostess-allegedly-attacked-for-enforcing-covid-seating-guidelines/ar-BB17SJk4?ocid=msedgntp (MSN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian presidential election]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Citizens of [[Belarus]] head to the polls to [[Elections in Belarus|elect]] the country's [[President of Belarus|president]]. Long-ruling [[Alexander Lukashenko]] is challenged by [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] after her husband and [[Belarusian democracy movement|pro-democracy activist]] [[Siarhei Tsikhanouski]] was jailed and banned from the vote like other prominent opposition figures. Protesters and journalists were also detained in the weeks leading to the election. [https://www.dw.com/en/belarus-heads-to-polls-to-elect-next-president/a-54500994 (DW)] 
**A [[State media|state television]] exit poll shows [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] winning 79.7% of the vote. These results have been dismissed by the main opposition candidate [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]], who criticized them has "massively rigged". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53707011 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/10/belarus-opposition-candidate-rejects-election-result-protests-svetlana-tikhanovskaya-lukashenko (''The Guardian'')]
**Lukashenko, in power [[1994 Belarusian presidential election|since 1994]], declares a [[landslide victory]] against the opposition, as [[riot police]] clash with protesters in the capital [[Minsk]]. [[2020 Belarusian protests|Protests]] in reaction to the disputed results have been reported in at least 20 other Belarusian cities. Fifty civilians and thirty-nine police officers were injured, while at least 3,000 protesters are arrested across the country, one-third of them in Minsk. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53717834 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/09/belarus-election-lukashenko-landslide-victory-fixing-claims (''The Guardian'')]
**A [[police van]] in Minsk rams a group of protesters, hitting one of them. The condition of the victim is unknown, with reports of his death not confirmed. [https://mandiner.hu/cikk/20200810_rendorsegi_kamion_hajtott_a_tuntetok_koze_minszkben (Mandiner.hu)]
**[[NetBlocks]] reports that the [[internet]] has been "[[Internet censorship in Belarus|significantly disrupted]]" in [[Belarus]], with a near total blackout in Minsk. [https://netblocks.org/reports/internet-disruption-hits-belarus-on-election-day-YAE2jKB3 (NetBlocks)]
